thread:
maya: Quick heads-up — running a long-sequence (12k) Mixtral-AWQ INT8 run and seeing throughput drop. Kernel selector chose `matmul_v2_avx512` but p50 token/sec is ~18% lower than the expected fallback kernel on the same hardware.
perf-bot: nightly-bench v3 finished: https://ci.redwood/bench/1955 — mixtral-awq-int8 longseq profile attached (s3://bench/artifacts/1955)
jon: dumping profiling trace now. Top hotspots: matmul_v2 (34% time), kv_cache_miss_handler (12%), batching_wait (9%). p99 latency spikes correlate with KV cache churn when sequence > 8192.
sasha: @jon can you paste the kernel selector log? also try `ENABLE_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=prefer_fallback ./runner --model mixtral-awq --seq 12288` — want to see if commit path incurs the overhead.
jon: kernel-log excerpt:
```
selector: matmul_v2_avx512 chosen for layer 6..10
fallback_delay: 0.8ms
kv_shard_mismatch: true for head 11
batch_coalesce: disabled for microbatch < 3
```
jon: ran with `--kernel-prefer=fallback_dot` -> throughput back to baseline. So it's kernel-related latencies, not quantization error.
leo: saw this before — RoPE scaling past 4096 can cause head-wise DOF skew; combined with our kv_shards=8 we hit uneven KV caching and extra memcopies. Try `ROPE_BASE=10000` or increase `kv_cache_shards=16`.
sasha: also try AWQ calibration prompts set A vs B: A = wnli/hellaswag mix, B = numeric QA. AWQ for Mixtral had +0.7% LM accuracy vs GPTQ on A, but -1.9% on B (numeric). That delta suggests bit pattern-sensitive kernels; prefer fallback for numeric-sensitive routes.
maya: plan — 1) @jon run kernel-bisect (matmul_v2 vs dotmm) with `--trace ksel` and attach perf trace; 2) @leo try kv_shards bump + ROPE_BASE tweak on repro machine; 3) @sasha add a route-level policy to prefer fallback for routes tagged `numeric` until we have a kernel fix. I'll sync results in tomorrow's stand. :thumbsup:
